label: fact
about: How the flights page is made, as data for the reader's panel (Dinis via incident.conductor@, 11 November ~23:38 UTC: a visual explanation of how the plane data is worked out). Two pipelines and one sum: aircraft (adsb.lol -> our poll -> filter -> frames and snapshots -> tracks -> the map), the wind field (Open-Meteo -> the map's arrows) and the crosswind arithmetic on the airports' METAR, with a worked example. Each step names its source, the time it was read and its numbers. Every step's label: fact (read from the source), derived (arithmetic on facts, the rule printed), hypothesis (a drawing or a judgement of ours).
not_a_warning_service: Not a warning service. No forecast or advice of ours. Your airline decides whether your flight runs: its site or app has the latest. For warnings follow IPMA and ANEPC.

steps.label: fact
steps.title: Receivers
steps.what: Aircraft broadcast their position, altitude, speed and callsign by ADS-B about twice a second. Volunteers' receivers on the ground hear them and send what they hear to adsb.lol, which merges it.
steps.limits: Coverage depends on where volunteers have receivers; far out over the Atlantic and low near the ground there are gaps. An aircraft not heard is not on the map, which does not mean it is not flying.

steps.label: fact
steps.title: Our poll
steps.what: We ask adsb.lol's public API for every aircraft within a circle, and keep the raw answer in our private vault with its sha256.
steps.limit_source: https://api.adsb.lol/docs (500 requests a day per IP without a key; the window resets at 00:00 UTC), read 2026-11-11T23:40:00Z
steps.before: from 22:23 UTC on 11 November: Lisbon 40 nm and Madeira 30 nm every 10 minutes (snapshots/)
steps.time_read: each frame's t (adsb.lol's own clock) and request.read (ours)

steps.label: derived
steps.title: Filter
steps.what: A callsign that is an airline's three-letter ICAO code followed by a flight number (TAP1234, RYR85AB) is an airline flight, kept with its callsign and aircraft type. Every other aircraft is kept only as an anonymous position: its emitter category (light, large, heavy, rotorcraft), position, altitude rounded to 100 ft, speed and track, with no callsign, address, registration or type. Aircraft whose owners asked to be withheld (PIA or LADD in adsb.lol's data) are dropped and only counted. Never kept for anyone: the ICAO24 address, the registration.
steps.rule: /^([A-Z]{3})(\d[0-9A-Z]{0,4})$/ and the three letters in our airline list (tools/flights-common.mjs, shared with incident.transport@)

steps.label: fact
steps.title: Frames and snapshots
steps.what: Each poll becomes one frame: one array per aircraft under a header of fields (compact, so an hour of frames stays under the repository's 256 KB a file). The earlier snapshots (40 nm and 30 nm, objects) continue every 10 and 20 minutes for incident.transport@'s counts near the airports.

steps.label: derived
steps.title: Tracks
steps.what: For each hour, each airline callsign's points from every frame it appears in: first and last seen, and its altitude, speed, heading and phase at the last point. Phase is arithmetic on the reported vertical rate: climbing above +300 ft/min, descending below -300, cruising level at or above 10,000 ft, level below it, on ground when reported so.

steps.label: fact
steps.title: The map
steps.what: The designer's map draws each frame's measured positions. Between two frames nothing is measured: a plane drawn moving between them, or a trail joining its points, is a drawing (hypothesis) and the map says so.

steps.label: evidence
steps.title: A weather model
steps.what: Open-Meteo's forecast API, best match for each point: the model's hourly analysis for past hours and its short-range forecast for later ones. A model's wind, not a measurement.

steps.label: evidence
steps.title: A lattice of points
steps.what: Wind at 10 m (speed, direction, gusts) and at 850 hPa (about 1,500 m), hourly, at points 0.5 degrees apart over boxes that hold the aircraft areas (0.25 degrees over a smaller box until 11 November 23:54 UTC).

steps.label: evidence
steps.title: Arrows
steps.what: Each point becomes an arrow pointing where the wind goes (the direction it blows from plus 180 degrees), longer when stronger. Hours after forecast_from are the model's forecast, and the map marks them.

steps.label: fact
steps.title: The airport's own report
steps.what: Every half hour the airport's weather station issues a METAR: the wind's direction (degrees true), speed and gusts in knots.
steps.source: https://aviationweather.gov/api/data/metar?ids=LPPT,LPMA&hours=60&format=json (IPMA's observations through the US NOAA Aviation Weather Center, public domain)

steps.label: fact
steps.title: The runway's heading
steps.what: Each runway end's true heading.

formula.crosswind_kt: |wind_kt x sin(angle)|, from the left or the right

worked_example.metar: METAR LPPT 111400Z 19029G40KT 3000 R20/0900 +RA BR FEW002 BKN007 FEW015TCU 19/19 Q0989 WS R20 NOSIG
worked_example.on_02: the same numbers as a tailwind: -28.4 kt (-39.1 kt in the gust)
steps: crosswind = 29 x sin(12) = 29 x 0.208 = 6.0 kt, from the left
in the 40 kt gust: 39.1 kt headwind, 8.3 kt crosswind

steps.label: hypothesis
steps.title: Which end the wind favours
steps.what: The end with the most headwind. Air traffic control chooses the runway; we state no limit and no advice.

steps.label: Headwind and crosswind
steps.what: angle = wind direction - runway heading ; headwind_kt = wind_kt x cos(angle) (negative = tailwind) ; crosswind_kt = |wind_kt x sin(angle)|, from the left or the right
